Sam (support): hey team, customer (acct: mid-market-42) reports repeated 403s for text.generate call. They say it started after we migrated their seats. They pasted a snippet, looks auth-y but keys are valid. They see \"invalid_api_key\" in the client app.

Priya (support): can you paste the raw curl/logs from the customer? which endpoint and API key id? also which plan they were on before/after migration? :thinking_face:

Sam (support): pasted below (redacting actual key) — request shows 403 with body `{"error":"permission_denied","message":"invalid_api_key"}`. They hit `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text.generate` with header `Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-****` and `x-account-id: acct-mid-42`. They say they were on Starter -> Standard migration earlier today.

Sam (support): ```
POST /v1/text.generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
X-Account-ID: acct-mid-42

{
  \"model\": \"open-rlhf-7b\",
  \"input\": \"Summarize...\"
}

Response: HTTP/1.1 403
{ \"error\": \"permission_denied\", \"message\": \"invalid_api_key\" }
```

Jared (eng-runtime): quick sanity checks — the error string `invalid_api_key` is our catch-all when entitlement check fails before auth-level validation. Not ideal. Is there an entitlement service trace (request_id) from the customer?

Sam (support): customer gave request_id `req_0a7f3b`. I grabbed logs from our gateway: shows entitlement-service returned `403` with code `plan_block` and `reason: plan_mismatch`.

Priya (support): ok so it's an entitlement gating case, not raw key revocation. Customer thinks it's auth because client sees `invalid_api_key`. Need to communicate clearly and give repro steps to them.

Nina (billing): we did seat migration db job at 11:07. There's a known eventual-consistency window between seat sync and entitlement index (approx 5–10m). Could be hitting that. The account should be Standard now but the index might still report Starter.

Sam (support): customer said issue persisted 30m after migration. Any other reasons entitlement might be stale? cache TTLs?

Jared (eng-runtime): possible layering: 1) migration updated billing service, 2) billing event emitted -> entitlement indexer picks up, 3) downstream cache (gateway prefix cache) might hold old policy for up to 20m. But 30m is long. Can you share the gateway logs for req_0a7f3b tail? Also what token scope does their key have? If key is org-scoped vs project-scoped we might evaluate different plan checks.

Sam (support): pasted gateway tail: ```
[2026-05-12T11:40:22Z] req_0a7f3b acct=acct-mid-42 auth_key_id=ak-9876 gateway.cache.hit=false entitlement.status=blocked entitlement.code=plan_block
[2026-05-12T11:40:22Z] returning 403 to client message=invalid_api_key
```

Priya (support): next steps for support: 1) tell customer this is an entitlement/plan block not key revocation, 2) ask them to retry after we flush their gateway cache / trigger entitlement refresh, 3) offer a short workaround: create a temporary API key on their account (if allowed) or re-auth via the console to refresh session.

Jared (eng-runtime): engineering action: I can push a small change to entitlement-service to return clearer error bodies (code `plan_block` and message `account_plan_limits`) instead of mapping to `invalid_api_key`. Also add a log line to the gateway to include billing_version in traces. Will open a PR.

Jared (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.redwood.internal/p/infra/entitlement-service/+/345 — patch adds explicit error payload and reduces gateway cache TTL for plan checks from 20m -> 2m for accounts in migration state. Planning a canary deploy to staging then prod.

deploy-bot: Deployment queued for entitlement-service:pr-345 — canary region: us-west-2, expected rollout 10m.

Priya (support): Sam, tell customer we'll: 1) flush their entitlement cache, 2) temporarily allow a retry, and 3) ETA for fix (clearer error + shorter cache TTL) ~ 30–45m. Also give them repro command to show it's entitlement not key.

Sam (support): sending this repro to customer now: 
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text.generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Account-ID: acct-mid-42" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-rlhf-7b","input":"test"}'

# if entitlement is blocking you'll see 403 + body {"error":"permission_denied","code":"plan_block"} after fix.
```

Nina (billing): I manually re-run the indexing job for acct-mid-42 and invalidated the cache for the account. Should be propagated now.

Sam (support): customer retried and reports success! calls succeeded, response returned 200. they said they saw 403 for ~32 minutes. They've accepted the explanation but asked if we can avoid the confusing `invalid_api_key` text.

Jared (eng-runtime): noted — tracking in bug RED-2041 to change mapping and improve observability. Also adding a short FAQ for support: \"How to tell entitlement 403 from invalid key\" with quick grep steps and a sample curl.

Priya (support): closing loop with customer: explained cause (plan gating during seat migration), actions taken (cache invalidation + index rerun + upcoming mapping fix), and mitigation (retry / create temp key). Customer thanked us and asked for postmortem note if this recurs.

Sam (support): marking resolved on ticket and linking to RED-2041. will add internal note in support playbook. :white_check_mark:

Jared (eng-runtime): follow-up — after the canary finishes I'll post the deploy status here.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded in us-west-2 for pr-345. No errors. Rolling to prod now.

Jared (eng-runtime): prod roll complete. mapping now returns structured error: `{"error":"permission_denied","code":"plan_block","message":"account plan does not allow this action"}`. Closing RED-2041 when docs and playbook PRs land.

Priya (support): great, adding playbook PR now with snippet for support agents to distinguish entitlement 403 vs auth 401/403.

Sam (support): thanks everyone — good coordinated fix. :raised_hands:
